- Error rate rose from 0.4% to 3.1% at peak.
- We see a handful of very long tail requests (~15s) that don't match the normal distribution.

This is impacting our external customers; can Redwood prioritize? We need a mitigation plan and ETA.

-Samantha

Subject: Re: Latency spike — initial triage findings

Marissa / Samantha — quick summary from the trace bundle:

Observations:
- Many of the long tails are coming from requests that share a common prefix set (long historical context) and are hitting the shared in-memory KV prefix cache.
- We see repeated eviction/repopulation cycles: the prefix cache TTL is short for this customer's traffic pattern which is producing cache churn and head-of-line (headlock) blocking on batch lanes.
- When a batch worker blocks on a cache miss and repopulates, concurrent requests queue behind it (HOL) causing the 15s tails; this cascades into queue build-up and upstream backpressure -> 504s.

Root cause hypothesis: the current KV cache policy for customer-profiles with long prefixes creates thrash under synchronized batch windows. The eviction and blocking path is serializing work for the batch lane.

Immediate mitigations we can attempt now (minutes):
- Temporarily increase prefix cache size and TTL for Nexline routing bucket (reduces eviction).
- Isolate Nexline onto a soft-dedicated lane with its own prefetch queue to avoid HOL impacts on shared lanes.
- Decrease max batch wait for the shared lane to force earlier partial flushes (trades cost for latency).

I'll apply the first change now (TTL bump + prefetch tuning) and monitor. Attaching a filtered trace that highlights the evictions.

Regards,
Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Marissa — please coordinate the customer comms. Evelyn, will you take point on the capacity request?

-Markus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nexline latency spike — proposed short-term plan

Samantha — quick update and proposed plan: we believe a combination of prefix-cache thrash and synchronized batch windows is producing head-of-line blocking in the shared batch lane.

Proposed immediate (short-term) actions — starting in 10 minutes, if you approve:
1) Increase prefix cache TTL for Nexline routes from 30s -> 300s and bump cache size by 2x.
2) Move Nexline to a soft-dedicated batch lane with +2 soft GPUs for 2 hours (no change to billing for this incident).
3) Reduce shared lane max_batch_wait from 100ms -> 40ms to avoid long in-queue blocking.
4) We'll monitor p50/p95/p99, error rate, and queue depth and share minute-by-minute for the first hour.

Tradeoffs: this will slightly increase token unit cost for Nexline during the window but should restore latency and eliminate the 504 cascade.

Please reply "approve" or propose an alternate window. If approved, we'll execute and confirm when stable.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success
